cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Pick a Priority
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Your parents' gravy needs stirring and you need a lift to the station. Which am I doing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you leave dinner on a timer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. It won't stir the gravy. Do I finish their dinner or drive you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finish dinner. I'll book a taxi. Just carry my suitcase downstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose again: suitcase downstairs now, or gravy without lumps for your parents?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 timer cannot stir is a real professional correction that shapes the forced choice, although generic wrappers weaken the voice.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 timer proposal causes A3 cooking correction; B4 taxi solves lift but introduces bag task, causing A5 fresh choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 try workable compromises rather than merely obstruct A.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes the helpful taxi plan reveal another demand competing with the same gravy.

specificity.evidence: A1 parents dinner and train lift provide immediate ordinary obligations.
